1  NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  MCRC No. 5505 of 2023 Pradeep Netam @ Lakhishwer Netam, S/o Bandhulal Netam, aged about 18 years, R/o Village Fukagirola, Police Thana Anantpur, District Kondagaon, Chhattisgarh.
---- Applicant  Versus State of Chhattisgarh through Police Station Anantpur, District Kondagaon, Chhattisgarh.

---- Non-Applicant For Applicant : Mr. Sanjay Yadav, Advocate For Non-Applicant/State : Mr. G.P. Kurre, P.L.
For Victim : Mr. Nitin Dewangan, Advocate  Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal  Order on Board 19.09.2023 1.
The applicant has moved this first bail application under Section 439 of Criminal Procedure Code for releasing him on regular bail during trial in connection with Crime No.11 of 2023 registered at Police Station Anantpur, District Kondagaon (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 457,
376(2)(n), 376(a)(b) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
2. Case of the prosecution, is that, mother of the victim lodged a report alleging therein that on 28.03.2023, her daughter was sleeping at her house.

sentences.text: On the basis of complaint, a case has been registered against Pradeep Netam alias Lakhishwar Netam at Police Station Anantapur.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in crime in question.
He would further submit that if the entire prosecution case is taken as it is, it appears that the victim is a consenting party.
It is contended that there was civil dispute between the parties and nothing has been mentioned in the MLC report.
It is further contended that trial may likely to take some time and applicant is in jail since 03.04.2023.

It is lastly contended that there is no likelihood of his case being decided in near future, therefore, present applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposing the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant and would submit that that there is ample evidence on record to connect the appellant with commission of aforesaid offence.
He would further submit that on the date of incident, prosecutrix was minor, i.e. aged about 15 years, hence, applicant is not entitled for grant of bail.
5. Father of the victim is present in person before this Court and he is having no objection in grant of bail to the applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

7. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations, there is ample evidence on record to connect the applicant with commission of offence, material available on record, particularly the fact that on the date of incident, prosecutrix was minor, i.e. aged about 15 years, I do not find it to be a fit case to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, bail application is rejected.

Sd/-/---
(Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal) Judge Yogesh Pradeep Netam @ Lakhishwer Netam vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90637190/
